design: Written for the open pack from real history; nothing comes from the original game. The order and fields are asset-packs.md's ("Open game data", data/scenarios): 24 careers, era by era (1560 ... 1680), each English, French, Dutch, Spanish; then the 6 famous expeditions in the order of the open text's expedition menu, in the eras the engine fixes for them (expedition_era in src/ui/screens.c: 1560, 1560, 1620, 1660, 1660, 1680). Relations. Per era, the four nations' state in the Caribbean during the era's first decade, the one a career mostly plays: "no peace beyond the line" meant the Spanish treated intruders as enemies whatever Europe's treaties said, so the war that defined the decade there wins over a peace that held only in Europe. An expedition takes the relations of its own year. -1 war, 0 peace, 1 alliance; symmetric. Careers. The player starts in a home port of his nation in the era, one of towns.py's towns of that nation, chosen to fit the career's story (stories.py) and its history. The four start cells are that town's own arrival cells within a cell of it, the most open water first: the engine (sim_new_game, start_town in src/sim/sim.c) puts the player in the town owning the arrival cell nearest the drawn start cell when that town is within 4 cells of it, then on the water outside its harbour. A career starts with one small ship, a few dozen men, a few guns, a modest purse and food for some months; the hold is the ship's (src/sim/internal.h, sim_ship_room: type x 2 + 2 tens of tons). The player's standing is 1 with his own nation, rank 1 (Ensign) there; with the others, their relation to his nation (-1 at war, 0 at peace, 1 allied), rank 0; pirates -1. Expeditions. The real voyage's force, cut to the engine's eight ships (the largest ones, or the eight a captain sailed in with), its men and guns in proportion; the date (years past the era's first x 360 + day of a 30-day-month year) and the months already at sea since the fleet's last port of call, when its Caribbean part began; the start at sea where it did, at least five cells from every town of the era, so the engine leaves the fleet on the open water (start_town finds no town). Home ports: 1560 england: Isla de Pinos; 1560 france: Fort Caroline; 1560 holland: Curacao; 1560 spain: Santo Domingo; 1600 england: St Lucia; 1600 france: Martinique; 1600 holland: Punta de Araya; 1600 spain: Havana; 1620 england: St Christopher; 1620 france: Guadeloupe; 1620 holland: Nieuw Walcheren; 1620 spain: Cartagena; 1640 england: Barbados; 1640 france: Tortuga; 1640 holland: Curacao; 1640 spain: San Juan; 1660 england: Port Royal; 1660 france: Petit-Goave; 1660 holland: St Eustatius; 1660 spain: Santiago de Cuba; 1680 england: Port Royal; 1680 france: Cap-Francois; 1680 holland: Curacao; 1680 spain: Havana.
